Des Moines holds countless untold stories within its historic buildings and neighborhoods. While the gleaming gold dome of the Iowa State Capitol catches every visitor's eye, the real treasures of our city's history often lie hidden in plain sight. Let's explore 12 fascinating historical spots that showcase the rich heritage of Iowa's capital city.

Underground Railroad Sites in Sherman Hill

Tucked away in the historic Sherman Hill neighborhood, several preserved homes once served as stops on the Underground Railroad. The Hoyt Sherman mansion, built in 1877, holds particular significance. While the mansion itself was constructed after the Civil War, the property's original structures played a crucial role in helping escaped enslaved people journey to freedom.

The Hidden Speakeasies of Court Avenue

Beneath the bustling Court Avenue Entertainment District lies a network of tunnels and basement spaces that once hosted some of Des Moines' most notorious Prohibition-era speakeasies. Today, several restaurants in the area have preserved these historic spaces, including the original bar at Django and the underground vault at Copper Cup.

Notable Speakeasy Sites:

  • The former Green Hat Club (now Americana)
  • The Underground Vault at 3rd and Court
  • The Historic Kirkwood Hotel basement

East Village's Industrial Heritage

Before becoming Des Moines' trendiest shopping and dining district, the East Village was the industrial heart of the city. The Des Moines Foundry Building, now home to Peace Tree Brewing, still bears witness to this era with its original brick walls and steel beams.
